papers.title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for reservoir cascade release scheduling: a climate-analytics evaluation of downstream low-flow equity under forecast uncertainty
papers.summary: Cascade reservoir operators must release water under uncertain inflow forecasts while satisfying competing demands for hydropower, irrigation and downstream environmental flows. The framework is formalised as a constrained Markov game with a lexicographic objective: maximise energy revenue subject to a probabilistic low-flow equity constraint at downstream reaches. A decomposed soft actor-critic architecture with a centralised equity critic is proposed, and a formal analysis establishes conditions under which the learned joint policy satisfies the equity constraint with high probability. papers.title: Image-based reinforcement learning for robust mode hop recovery in external-cavity diode lasers
papers.summary: Abstract Conventional laser frequency stabilization techniques such as table-lookup or heuristic methods have significant limitations due to intrinsic hysteresis and stochastic mode competition. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a simple hysteresis-aware protocol and a tailored image-based reinforcement learning (RL) framework. This approach enables robust mode hop recovery in external-cavity diode lasers (ECDLs). papers.title: Multi-criteria prioritized reinforcement learning for autonomous underwater vehicle navigation in 3D multi-node environments
papers.summary: Abstract Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are increasingly used as mobile data collectors in underwater wireless sensor networks, where navigation must balance task completion, obstacle avoidance, communication performance, and energy efficiency. This study develops a Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient framework with Multi-Criteria Prioritized Experience Replay (MC-PER-TD3). papers.title: Degradation-Aware Deep Reinforcement Learning for Battery Energy Storage Dispatch in Industrial Microgrids and Its Real-Time Deployment Validation
papers.summary: Battery degradation is a non-negligible cost in battery energy storage (BESS) dispatch for industrial microgrids, yet most deep reinforcement learning (DRL) studies optimize only the procurement cost. This paper embeds a rainflow-calibrated cyclic aging cost into the reward of a degradation-aware soft actor-critic (DA-SAC) framework with an adjustable weight λ, making the cost–lifetime trade-off explicit. papers.title: Evaluating Xception with Multitask Self-Supervised Learning for AI-Generated Image and Deepfake Video Detection
papers.summary: This study evaluates an Xception-based Multitask Self-Supervised Learning (MSSL) framework for detecting real and synthetic visual content across image and video modalities. Separate models were developed for CIFAKE images and FaceForensics++ videos. Beyond the primary binary-classification objective, MSSL integrates three auxiliary representation-learning tasks: rotation prediction, patch reconstruction, and artifact-map prediction. papers.title: Hearing the shape of an arena with spectral swarm robotics
papers.summary: Swarm robotics relies on robots with minimal sensing and computation that achieve self-organization at the level of the collective to address a variety of tasks. Yet, swarm robotics still struggles with global tasks that require understanding the broader spatial context in which robots operate, such as identifying the shape of the arena in which they are embedded. papers.title: WSM-Aware HRI: An IoT-Enhanced Framework for Early Detection and Norm-Guided Repair of Failures with LLM Guidance
papers.summary: Human–robot interaction (HRI) failures remain a major barrier to deploying robots in real-world environments. Prior work often treats failures as isolated technical faults or focuses on post-hoc recovery behaviors. In practice, many breakdowns arise because humans and robots operate under inconsistent assumptions about the current world state. papers.title: Navigation System for Wheeled Robots Using SLAM GMapping and LiDAR
papers.summary: One of the primary challenges in developing autonomous robots is enabling them to operate in dynamic, unstructured environments, where traditional navigation methods often fail. For instance, self-driving cars must continuously adapt to changing road conditions, traffic, and unexpected obstacles. In this context, efficient sensors and computing systems play a vital role. LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) technology has proven highly effective for autonomous robots, particularly for environmental mapping and obstacle avoidance. papers.title: Traditional methods for hand gesture recognition in video streams: overview and comparative characteristics
papers.summary: Hand gesture recognition is a relevant and promising field of research at the intersection of computer vision, robotics, and human-computer interaction. The article examines the key challenges faced by modern machine learning and computer vision algorithms in the analysis and classification of gestures. The paper provides a comparative analysis of traditional methods for describing gesture shapes, with a systematization of their advantages and disadvantages presented in tabular form.

papers.title: Semantically Grounded Explainability for Pedestrian Detection Using Anatomical Proportions and Grid-Based Visualization
papers.summary: Explainable computer vision aims to understand how and why complex vision systems make decisions. However, existing explainability methods often highlight relevant image regions without providing semantically meaningful explanations for human users. In this work, we analyze the behavior of a pedestrian detector under semantically meaningful image perturbations. papers.title: A Multimodal Framework for English-to-Indian Sign Language Translation from Online Video Using a Transition-Aware 3D Avatar with Adjustable Signing Speed
papers.summary: This research presents a proposed multimodal framework for continuous Indian Sign Language (ISL) translation and avatar-based sign production. The framework aims to improve communication accessibility by connecting sign-language recognition, language translation, and visual sign generation within a unified system. The proposed approach combines visual and temporal information, including hand gestures, body posture, facial expressions, and movement sequences, to support the interpretation of continuous signing. papers.title: From Games to Frictional Markets: How Experience Organization Governs the Transfer of a Self-Evolving RL Model
papers.summary: Learning from experience in the real world requires reinforcement-learning rules that remain effective when environments change and actions incur economic costs. Disco103, a state-of-the-art self-discovered RL rule from games, provides a strong starting point for this transfer problem. papers.title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for coordinated reservoir releases under conflicting hydropower and irrigation mandates: a climate-analytics evaluation of Pareto-regret and downstream equity
papers.summary: Reservoir operators in transboundary basins face a structural conflict: hydropower revenue is maximised by releasing water when electricity prices peak, while irrigation mandates require deliveries timed to crop water demand. papers.summary: Egg fertility assessment is essential for improving hatchery efficiency, reducing incubation costs, and minimizing resource waste caused by infertile eggs. This study aims to develop a computer vision-based framework for three-level egg fertility classification, namely Highly Fertile, Fertile, and Infertile. A balanced dataset consisting of 1,500 manually collected candling images (500 images per class) was validated by three poultry experts.
